issues.problem:
A Wedge written another way outranks its original by one ulp of volume, so an invisible copy takes a tip out of the Blade.

A Wedge (sx, sy, sz) is the same solid as (sx, sz, sy) turned a half turn about its local (0, 1, -1); the world vertices come out bit-identical. Shapes.prepare's volume 4*hx*hy*hz rounds the two writings an ulp apart. Over 10,000 random sizes the other writing's volume is larger in 17.3 %, smaller in 18.0 % and equal in 64.7 %. Sampling.ranked (lines 489-495) sorts Blocks' extents but compares a Wedge's raw volume before the slot's name.

F4 + its tip written the other way in the Guard: the copy (0.027200000000000002 against 0.027199999999999998) ranks 3rd against the tip's 4th. The copy is kept, the tip cleaned, and Sharpening goes 0.3420 Hard -> 0.1814 Normal through the emulator. C08 + either tip: 0.2487 Hard -> 0.0076 Normal. The copies of F3's, C02's, C04-C06's and C09's tips tie and are cleaned.

This makes these statements false:
- §4.4: a copy in a later slot, its size written another way, is cleaned and changes nothing.
- §17.1 O8 and §17.2: no copy of one volume can take a part out of the Blade, whatever the size's writing.
- §5.6, the same row.

Verdict.spec only pins Blocks.

issues.problem:
§4.4 says "the probe is conservative", but it is not against a thin hider.

A round facet probes HIDE_OFFSET + its sag along its normal. Near its vertices that lands up to sag*(1 + δ/r) past its true points' probes. Where the hider ends between the two, the truth's probe stays inside it and the model's leaves it.

Example (m2x-v1-3/cap2.luau): a Ball r 0.3 buried in a block but for a top cap 0.004 to 0.008 high, the cap under a Wedge whose thickness over the pole is 0.013 to 0.015. It reads 0.11 to 0.22 % where the truth reads 0.00 to 0.09 %; at r 0.25 it reads 0.08 % against 0. That is per such cap. I found no verdict it moves, and only a Wedge's or CornerWedge's thin edge can be that thin, since MIN_DIM is 0.02.

summary:
M2 fails this round: 1 blocker and 1 major. The change otherwise holds up: the reading is exact on its model, orders and copies change nothing, and the cap and checkpoints behave as stated. I edited only copies under m2x-v1-3; the repo is untouched.

The blocker: a part wholly inside a Ball or Cylinder, against its true surface, is read as showing and kept. Against a round hider, Cover's buried piece uses the inscribed model (line 827). A face inside the true surface but outside that model, facing out, therefore reads as showing, while the truth buries it.
- F5 with its pommel a Ball 0.6 across, plus 4 Blade Blocks inside it: each reads 10 % against a truth of 0, and Sharpening goes 0.0989 Normal to 0.2169 Hard.
- Blade Balls inside the same pommel take it to 0.2958 Hard.
- A plate inside a Cylinder reads 20–30 %.
- This makes §5's "hidden filler cannot move a tier" false, and §17.2 does not list it.

My tried fix, fixAB, has two parts:
- Flat facets use the round hider's half-spaces moved out to its true surface.
- A round facet whose true patch lies wholly inside a round hider is hidden whole.

fixAB results:
- Every attack is cleaned.
- 0 verdicts move on the 33,389 plausible designs, the fixtures and the attack designs.
- The suite passes but for one units pin.
- Timing is unchanged.
- Its price: blocks poking 0.001–0.002 out of a Ball's pole read hidden where the truth shows 5–8 %.

The major: a Wedge written as (sx, sz, sy) turned a half turn about its local (0, 1, −1) is the same solid, but its rank volume differs by one ulp. That lets an invisible copy in the Guard take the tip out of the Blade: F4's Sharpening goes 0.3420 Hard to 0.1814 Normal, and C08's 0.2487 Hard to 0.0076 Normal. This contradicts §4.4 and O8. One line in Sampling.ranked fixes it (suite 589/0/0), and a new test fails on the build and passes with the fix.

Minors:
- The probe is not conservative against a thin hider (about 0.1–0.2 % per cap).
- "Up to 41.8 %" for the tied-axis copy is really 47.3 % for another rod.
- 16 surviving mutants in the cap stop and report cadence; 3 new tests kill them.

What holds:
- Exactness: 1,550 tangles against my independent brute force, 0 errors outside the tie bracket, nothing non-finite.
- Bit-identical across random orders, exact copies placed first or last, and Dust.
- Measure bit-identical to the round-1 base wherever verdicts agree (1,407 designs).
- The cap: reports stop right after it is passed, the largest single report is 3,570 units, and 288 raised checkpoints leave no state.
- Timing on a quiet machine is within §4.9's numbers, and every checkpoint gap is under 0.35 ms.
- The determinism rules hold.
